issues.description: Element: Lecture constructor. Problem statement (task description) and the reference solution expect a constructor that initializes all five attributes in the UML order: (String lectureName, int numberOfInscribedStudents, int numberOfGuestStudents, int numberOfLecturers, int numberOfTutors). The template repository instead provides a constructor with only three parameters: (String lectureName, int numberOfInscribedStudents, int numberOfGuestStudents) (template/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java signature at line 7). This mismatch between the required five-parameter constructor and the template's three-parameter constructor will confuse students about the required signature and order and can cause compilation or test failures when automated tests or example usages expect the five-argument constructor.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template constructor match the UML and the solution: replace the three-parameter constructor with the five-parameter constructor in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java: public Lecture(String lectureName, int numberOfInscribedStudents, int numberOfGuestStudents, int numberOfLecturers, int numberOfTutors) and initialize the five attributes in that exact order. Alternatively, remove the incorrect three-argument constructor from the template so students implement the required five-argument constructor themselves. Ensure the template's constructor signature and the problem statement's wording remain consistent.
